title: The Tabernacle
buttonText: Show the parts of the tabernacle
intro: God gives Moses detailed instructions for building the tabernacle—a portable sanctuary where God could dwell in the midst of His people. Each element carried deep symbolic meaning and pointed forward to Christ.

items.title: Gifts from the People
items.text: Gold, silver, bronze, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, red-dyed ram skins, badger skins, acacia wood, oil, spices, and precious stones.

items.title: The Ark of the Covenant
items.text: A chest made of acacia wood, measuring 2.5 by 1.5 by 1.5 cubits, overlaid with pure gold inside and out. The tablets of the covenant were to be kept here.

items.title: The Mercy Seat
items.text: A cover made of pure gold with two cherubim facing each other, their wings spread out over the cover. Here God would meet with Moses.

items.title: The Table of Showbread
items.text: A table made of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with plates, bowls, pitchers, and cups. The twelve loaves of showbread were to always stand before the Lord.

items.title: The Seven-Branched Lampstand
items.text: A lampstand (menorah) made of pure gold with seven branches, decorated with almond blossoms. It symbolizes God's light and presence.

footer.title: Christ in the Tabernacle
footer.content: The tabernacle points to Jesus: He is the way (the entrance), the truth (the ark with the law), and the life (the mercy seat). The book of Hebrews explains how Jesus fulfilled all that the tabernacle symbolized.
